summary: Shannon County, MO: 60-ft wooden tower dedicated Jan 1945 near Round Spring; a 100-ft steel tower erected 1967; no source confirms its 2026 condition.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an observation cabin at the top (NGS description); the first tower was a 60-foot wooden structure dedicated in 1945
facts.status_note: No source read confirms the tower's condition in 2026. The NGS description is credited to a 1963 survey.

staffing.status: Towerman's residence built at the site (fiscal 1950-51 report; another residence noted in 1962)

facts.agency: Missouri Conservation Commission (later reports name the Missouri Department of Conservation)

visit.trail_note: NGS directions end with a sharp left turn and a 0.35-mile run from a side road to the tower; the description is old, so the route may have changed

events.note: Towersite land acquired (49 acres per a state report); footings poured in October 1944
60-foot wooden tower dedicated January 7, 1945 on land donated by the Pioneer Cooperage Company

Major repairs to the tower (fiscal 1956-57 report)

National Geodetic Survey station description, credited to a 1963 survey, describes a steel tower about 100 feet tall
A 100-foot steel tower erected; the reports do not say whether it replaced the 60-foot wooden tower
Garage at the towersite received new siding (fiscal 1969-70)
New entrance cable, porch, roof and storm sash installed (fiscal 1971-72)
Room addition completed at the tower residence (fiscal 1977-78)
Bathroom work completed at the tower residence (fiscal 1980-81)

corrections.why: 18.3 m is 60 feet, the height of the 1945 wooden tower. The 1967 steel tower is 100 feet per the state reports, and the NGS description says about 100 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's 18.3 m matches the original 60-foot wooden tower. The later 100-foot steel tower is the structure both the state reports (1967) and the NGS description point to, so 30.5 m is used.

sources.title: Datasheet for station HC0806, Shannondale Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Current (2026) condition and public access not confirmed by any readable source; the brief's status stays unknown. Unresolved: the NGS description is credited to a 1963 survey yet describes a steel tower, four years before the state's 1967 steel tower; the acreage figures differ (49, 50, 40). Facebook posts from the Missouri Conservation History page and a Missouri Life article (HTTP 403) were not usable, so neither is cited. The 1967 entry does not say whether the steel tower replaced the wooden one. Visit.climbable and access.level left unset.
